sections.heading: 3.1 Architecture Overview
sections.text: We redesign the fundamental building block of the Transformer to explicitly separate feature generation from feature propagation . As illustrated in Figure 1 , the proposed Manifold-Geometric Transformer (MGT) Block deviates from the standard Post-LN structure by introducing a geometric processing stage before the residual addition. The forward pass of an MGT layer l is decomposed into three distinct phases: 1. Raw Feature Generation: First, the input state \mathbf{X}_{l} is normalized and processed by a standard mixing module (Multi-Head Self-Attention or Feed-Forward Network) to generate a candidate update vector \mathbf{V}_{raw}. 2. Geometric Rectification (via mHC): Instead of direct addition, \mathbf{V}_{raw} is passed through the Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connection (mHC) module. This module acts as a spatial filter, projecting the raw update onto the estimated tangent space of the data manifold. 3. Delta Dynamics (via DDL): Finally, the Deep Delta Learning (DDL) controller computes a dynamic gating scalar \bm{\beta} based on the input context \mathbf{X}_{l}. This scalar modulates the rectified vector. Crucially, to strictly approximate a geometric reflection, we include a subtraction term proportional to the current state projection, allowing for true ”erasure” mechanics. Input State \mathbf{X}_{l} LayerNorm MHSA / FFN (\mathbf{V}_{raw}) mHC Projection (\Psi) \times + Output \mathbf{X}_{l+1} DDL Gate \beta(\mathbf{X}_{l}) Raw Rectified Gate \beta Phase 2: Geometry Phase 3: Dynamics Figure 1: Architecture of the Manifold-Geometric Transformer (MGT) Block. The pipeline explicitly separates (1) feature generation, (2) geometric rectification (blue/purple), and (3) dynamic erasure (orange). The dashed orange line illustrates the context-aware gating mechanism derived directly from the input state.

sections.heading: 3.2 Preliminaries: The Manifold Hypothesis in Deep Layers
sections.text: Let \mathcal{X}=\{\mathbf{x}_{l}\}_{l=0}^{L} denote the sequence of hidden states in a Transformer, where \mathbf{x}_{l}\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times D}. We posit that valid semantic representations do not populate the entire Euclidean space \mathbb{R}^{D}, but rather lie on a lower-dimensional Riemannian manifold \mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}. A naive step \mathbf{x}_{l}+\mathbf{v}_{l} often forces the representation off the manifold (\mathbf{x}_{l+1}\notin\mathcal{M}). To maintain structural integrity, the update vector must be constrained to the local tangent space T_{\mathbf{x}_{l}}\mathcal{M}.

sections.heading: 3.3 Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC)
sections.text: The goal of mHC is to rectify the raw update vector \mathbf{v}_{raw} generated by the sub-layers (MHSA or FFN). Since computing the exact tangent space via eigendecomposition is computationally prohibitive, we employ an efficient Soft Subspace Approximation . We define the mHC operator \Psi(\cdot) as a learnable gating mechanism that approximates orthogonal projection: \mathbf{v}_{mHC}=\mathbf{v}_{raw}\odot\sigma(\text{LN}(\mathbf{W}_{gate}\mathbf{x}_{l})) (1) where \mathbf{W}_{gate} projects the input to a semantic importance score. While not a strict orthogonal projection in the linear algebra sense, this acts as a soft manifold constraint, suppressing feature dimensions (noise subspace) that deviate from the current semantic trajectory defined by \mathbf{x}_{l}.

sections.heading: 3.4 Deep Delta Learning (DDL): The Geometric Update Law
sections.text: Once the update direction is rectified by mHC, we must determine the update dynamics . Standard connections assume a fixed step size. To enable true erasure (moving backwards along the current state vector), we adopt the generalized Householder form ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) . We introduce the Delta Controller \beta(\mathbf{x}_{l}): \bm{\beta}=\lambda\cdot\tanh(\mathcal{G}(\mathbf{x}_{l}))+\epsilon (2) where \mathcal{G}(\cdot) is a lightweight linear projection. The Generalized Householder Update: To strictly implement the geometric capability of ”erasing” the current state information, the update rule must include a subtractive term proportional to the current state. We formulate the final update as: \mathbf{x}_{l+1}=\mathbf{x}_{l}+\bm{\beta}\odot(\mathbf{v}_{mHC}-\alpha\cdot\text{Proj}_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x}_{l})) (3) In our simplified implementation, we approximate the projection term \text{Proj}_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{x}_{l}) with the normalized state itself, governed by a learnable scalar \alpha. This formulation allows: • Accumulation: When \beta>0 and \mathbf{v}_{mHC} dominates. • Erasure/Reflection: When \beta scales the negative term -\alpha\mathbf{x}_{l}, effectively subtracting current features from the residual stream (Householder-like reflection).

sections.heading: 3.5 Algorithm
sections.text: Algorithm 1 summarizes the forward pass of a single MGT block. The procedure explicitly separates the four computational phases: (1) standard feature extraction via LayerNorm and the mixing sub-layer, (2) geometric rectification through the mHC projection, (3) dynamic gate computation via the DDL controller, and (4) the final Householder-style update that combines the rectified features with the erasure term. This modular decomposition enables independent analysis of each component’s contribution and facilitates efficient ablation studies. Algorithm 1 Forward Pass of Manifold-Geometric Transformer Block 0: Input state \mathbf{X}_{l}\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times D}, Sub-layer \mathcal{F} 0: Updated state \mathbf{X}_{l+1} 1: 1. Raw Generation 2: \tilde{\mathbf{X}}_{l}\leftarrow\text{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{X}_{l}) 3: \mathbf{V}_{raw}\leftarrow\mathcal{F}(\tilde{\mathbf{X}}_{l}) # Compute standard attention/FFN update 4: 2. mHC Projection (Geometry) 5: \mathbf{G}_{manifold}\leftarrow\sigma(\mathbf{X}_{l}\mathbf{W}_{m}+\mathbf{b}_{m}) # Soft approximation of tangent constraint 6: \mathbf{V}_{mHC}\leftarrow\mathbf{V}_{raw}\odot\mathbf{G}_{manifold} # Project update onto valid manifold 7: 3. DDL Dynamics (Kinematics) 8: \mathbf{H}_{geo}\leftarrow\mathbf{X}_{l}\mathbf{W}_{d}+\mathbf{b}_{d} 9: \bm{\beta}\leftarrow\lambda\cdot\tanh(\mathbf{H}_{geo}) # Determine step size & sign 10: 4. Geometric Update (Householder) 11: \mathbf{V}_{delta}\leftarrow\mathbf{V}_{mHC}-\alpha\cdot\mathbf{X}_{l} # Include explicit state subtraction term 12: \mathbf{X}_{l+1}\leftarrow\mathbf{X}_{l}+\bm{\beta}\odot\mathbf{V}_{delta} # Execute generalized reflection/update 13: return \mathbf{X}_{l+1}

sections.heading: 4 Proposed Evaluation Framework
sections.text: We design a comprehensive experimental protocol consisting of five experiments to rigorously validate the Manifold-Geometric Transformer (MGT). The goal is not merely to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy, but to falsify our core hypothesis: that constraining updates to the tangent space while enabling erasure dynamics leads to superior signal propagation in deep networks.

sections.heading: 4.1 Experimental Setup
sections.text: Datasets. We evaluate on language modeling benchmarks: • WikiText-2/103: Standard language modeling benchmarks for measuring perplexity and training dynamics. • Synthetic Copy Task: A controlled task where the model must copy the first half of the sequence to the second half, enabling precise analysis of information flow. Baselines. To isolate the contribution of MGT components: • Standard: Post-LN Transformer as the control group. • +mHC Only: Standard Transformer augmented with mHC projection. • +DDL Only: Standard Transformer augmented with DDL dynamics. • MGT (Full): Complete architecture with both mHC and DDL.
